questions.text:
A student wrote two context-free grammars G1 and G2 for generating a single C-like array declaration. The dimension of the array is at least one. For example,
int a[10][3];
The grammars use D as the start symbol,and use six terminal symbols int ;id[]num.

Which of the grammars correctly generate the declaration mentioned above?
questions.solution:
Derive int a[10][3]; with each grammar:
- G1: D [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int L; [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int id [ E ; [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int id [ num ] [ E ; [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int id [num] [num] ; True
- G2: D [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int L; [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int id E ; [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int id E [num] ; [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int id [num] [num] ; True

Both also give one or more dimensions in general.

Answer: Both G1 and G2

questions.text:
Consider the following processes, with the arrival time and the length of the CPU burst given in milli seconds.The scheduling algorithm used is preemptive shortest remaining-time first.

The average turn around time of these processes is milliseconds.
questions.solution:
SRTF: P1 0-3 (7 left); P2 arrives (6 [latex]\lt[/latex] 7) and runs 3-7 (2 left); P3 (1) runs 7-8; P2 runs 8-10; P4 runs 10-13; P1 runs 13-20.

Turnaround: P1 20, P2 10 [latex]-[/latex] 3 = 7, P3 8 [latex]-[/latex] 7 = 1, P4 13 [latex]-[/latex] 8 = 5.

Average = 33 / 4 = 8.25

Answer: 8.25

questions.text:
Consider the following two-process synchronization solution.


The shared variable turn is initialized to zero.Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
This is strict alternation: the processes must take turns. Mutual exclusion holds, but if process 0 wants to enter twice while process 1 does not want to enter at all, process 0 is blocked (turn = 1) by a process that is not even trying. That violates progress.

Answer: This solution violates progress requirement

questions.text: Consider a non-negative counting semaphore S. The operation P(S) decrements S, and V(S) increments S. During an execution, 20 P(S) operations and 12V(S) operations are issued in some order. The largest initial value of S for which at least one P(S) operation will remain blocked is ________.
questions.solution:
With initial value x, the 12 V operations can supply at most 12 more units, so at most x + 12 P operations can succeed. For at least one of the 20 P operations to stay blocked: [latex]x+12 \lt 20\Rightarrow x\le7[/latex].

Answer: 7

questions.text:
A file system uses an in-memory cache to cache disk blocks.The miss rate of the cache is shown in the figure. The latency to read a block from the cache is 1 ms and to read a block from the disk is 10ms. Assume that the cost of checking whether a block exists in the cache is negligible. Available cache sizes are in multiples of 10MB.

The smallest cache size required to ensure an average read latency of less than 6ms is_________ MB.
questions.solution:
Average latency = (1 [latex]-[/latex] m) [latex]\times[/latex] 1 + m [latex]\times[/latex] 10 = 1 + 9m (m = miss rate). We need [latex]1+9m \lt 6\Rightarrow m \lt 0.556[/latex].

From the graph: 20 MB gives 60% (too high), 30 MB gives 40% [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] latency 1 + 3.6 = 4.6 ms True

Answer: 30
